source: Transcribed from the Siglent SDM Series Digital Multimeter Programming Guide (EN02A). Standard SCPI — not Siglent's generator dialect. The Scanner category is the guide's ROUTe subsystem and needs the scanner card an -SC model carries. On an SDM3065X without one they do not report an error — they do not answer at all, and the link has to be rebuilt afterwards; ROUTe:IMPedance? and ROUTe:TEMPerature:TRANsducer? were the only two commands in a bench sweep of this catalog that behaved that way. Where the guide writes one entry with an alternation this catalog writes the branches out: MEASure[:VOLTage]:{AC|DC}?, MEASure:CURRent:{AC|DC}?, MEASure:{RESistance|FRESistance}? and MEASure:{FREQuency|PERiod}? become eight entries, six of which the guide's own short-form examples print separately anyway (MEAS:VOLT:DC?, MEAS:RES?, MEAS:FREQ? and so on). ROUTe:TEMPerature:TRANsducer? is the long form of the guide's ROUT:TEMP:TRAN?, which is the only spelling it prints. *OPC? appears nowhere in the guide and is kept as a mandatory IEEE 488.2 command, the same call the Siglent scope catalog makes.

commands.guideMisprint: The guide disagrees with itself here and the instrument settled it on 11 August 2026. Its §6.5 command summary prints this node as {UDEFine|MDEFine} while the contents page, the §6.5.5-7 headings, the parameter tables and every example print MDEFine alone. An SDM3065X answers both: TEMP:UDEF:RTD:TRAN:LIST? and TEMP:UDEF:THER:TRAN:LIST? return NONE with a clean error queue, against PT100,PT1000 for the MDEF form. The summary is right and the headings are incomplete, so the alternation is what this catalog carries.
